function: Predictive beamforming: DDCT (CNN plus transformer) selects the next-interval Type I codebook beam from historical delay-Doppler CSI of an OTFS downlink (p. 8-9).
system: MISO OTFS downlink in FDD: BS with Ntx=2A1A2 antenna ports (16 in tests), single-antenna vehicles at 100 km/h, 5.9 GHz, no RIS (p. 3, 6, 11).
method: CNN projection per CSI matrix plus one-layer transformer encoder (2 heads, hidden 16), softmax over codebook beams; cross-entropy loss, supervised paradigm implied, labels not described (p. 8-9).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa-generated east-west highway (3 lanes per direction, BS 300 m from road centre), LOS and NLOS; own simulated dataset, number of samples not stated (p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained on 2 cars per direction, tested on 2 other cars of the same highway scenario; DL comparisons use 16 antennas, LOS and NLOS (p. 9, 11).
baselines: Learned: DNN (4-layer), ConvLSTM, 3DCNN (p. 9); non-learned: no beamforming and optimal beamforming, the best codebook beam per sampling point (p. 12).
metrics: Average RSS, CDF of RSS, rank distribution of the beam selected, BER versus SNR with estimated and perfect CSI (p. 10-12).
q1_support: p. 9: "quasi deterministic radio channel generator (Quadriga)" simulates the vehicular channels, LOS and NLOS; QuaDRiGa is a shared channel model, and the paper does not name the 3GPP scenario.
q2_support: p. 9: "for training, and 2 of the remaining cars with different" directions are used for testing; held-out cars of the same QuaDRiGa highway scenario, and DL comparisons use only the 16-antenna case (p. 11).
q3_support: p. 12: "of none beamforming, optimal beamforming, and the" DDCT-based predictive beamforming, compared by mean RSS in Fig. 12; p. 9: "ConvLSTM: a neural network architecture that combines" CNN and LSTM, with DNN and 3DCNN, as learned baselines.
q4_support: p. 9: "a hidden dimension of 16 with a kernel size of (5, 9), while" the transformer has 2 heads; only hyperparameters are given, with no parameter count, FLOPs or runtime for DDCT anywhere in the paper.
q5_support: p. 9: "quasi deterministic radio channel generator (Quadriga)" produces the self-simulated dataset; no code or data link, and no public or measured dataset, is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 3 rather than 4: the system is OTFS, but the learned function is predictive beam selection, while the DD-domain channel estimation and MRC detection are classical (p. 6-7). The non-learned references in q3 are no beamforming and the oracle optimal codebook beam; the reviewer may confirm that they suffice. q2 is 0 because the test cars are held out from the same QuaDRiGa highway scenario.
